question.question: Could you please explain the complete process of performing an Advance Move, including how the distance is determined and what restrictions are imposed on a unit that performs this action, so I can better plan my tactical maneuvers?
question.reference: When a unit Advances, an Advance roll is made for that unit by rolling one D6. The result in inches from this roll is then added to the Move characteristic of each model in that unit until the end of the phase. Each model in that unit can then make an Advance move by moving a distance in inches less than or equal to this total, meaning models move up to M+D6". However, there are specific restrictions: no model can be moved within Engagement Range of any enemy models, and a unit that Advanced cannot shoot or declare a charge in the same turn.

### Source, Version, and Scope
* **Source:** Warhammer 40,000 Core Rules (10th Edition) [Core Rules p. 9, 13, 14, 15, 17, 25, 41, 54] and Core Stratagem records [DB: stratagems].
* **Supplied Facts:** The user requested the full procedure for making an Advance Move, how distance is determined, and all imposed restrictions.
* **Established Facts:** The rules for selecting units to move, making an Advance roll, model movement, and subsequent restrictions/exceptions on shooting, charging, and Engagement Range are established by the Core Rules citations below.

---

### Process and Rules for an Advance Move

#### 1. Eligibility and Timing
* **Phase & Step:** Performed during the **1. Move Units** step of the Movement phase [Core Rules p. 13].
* **Eligibility:**
  * When selecting a unit on the battlefield to move, it can make a Normal move, an Advance, or Remain Stationary **unless** that unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models [Core Rules p. 13].
  * If a unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can only Remain Stationary or Fall Back [Core Rules p. 13].
  * *Aircraft Exception:* If the *only* enemy models within Engagement Range of the unit are Aircraft models, the unit can still make a Normal move or an Advance move [Core Rules p. 54].

#### 2. Determining the Distance
1. **Advance Roll:** Roll one D6 for the advancing unit [Core Rules p. 14].
2. **Calculate Distance:** Add the result of the D6 (in inches) to the Move (M) characteristic of each model in that unit until the end of the phase [Core Rules p. 14].
3. **Re-rolls:** 
   * A player may spend 1 CP to use the core Stratagem **Command Re-roll** immediately after making an Advance roll to re-roll the die [Core Rules p. 41; DB: stratagems].
   * Re-rolls apply before any modifiers, and a die can never be re-rolled more than once [Core Rules p. 9].

#### 3. Moving the Models
* **Distance:** Each model in the unit can move a distance in inches less than or equal to the combined total ($\text{Move characteristic} + \text{Advance roll}$) [Core Rules p. 14].
* **Path & Positioning:**
  * Models can pivot and change position along any path, measured using the part of the base (or model, if it lacks a base) that moves furthest [Core Rules p. 13].
  * Models cannot cross the battlefield edge and cannot move across enemy models [Core Rules p. 13] (unless the moving model has the **Fly** keyword or is moving over enemy Aircraft [Core Rules p. 15, 54]).
  * Models can move over friendly models (other than Monster or Vehicle models moving over friendly Monster or Vehicle models), but cannot end their move on top of another model [Core Rules p. 13].

---

### Restrictions and Exceptions

1. **Engagement Range:**
   * **General Rule:** No model can be moved within Engagement Range of any enemy models at any point during or at the end of an Advance move [Core Rules p. 14].
   * **Fly / Aircraft Exception:** Models with **Fly** or models moving over enemy **Aircraft** can move within Engagement Range of enemy models/Aircraft during the move, but they cannot end their move within Engagement Range of any enemy model [Core Rules p. 15, 54].

2. **Shooting Restrictions:**
   * **General Rule:** A unit cannot shoot in the same turn that it Advanced [Core Rules p. 14].
   * **Assault Weapons Exception:** If an Advanced unit contains any models equipped with **Assault** (`[ASSAULT]`) weapons, the unit is still eligible to shoot in that turn's Shooting phase; however, it can only make attacks using its models' Assault weapons [Core Rules p. 25].

3. **Charging Restrictions:**
   * A unit cannot declare a charge in the same turn that it Advanced [Core Rules p. 14].

4. **Embarking Option:**
   * If every model in the unit ends its Advance move within 3" of a friendly Transport, the unit is permitted to embark inside that Transport (provided it did not already disembark from a Transport in that same phase) [Core Rules p. 17].

---

### Conclusion & Evidence Gap
All conditions, measurement steps, and restrictions governing Advance moves are defined in the 10th Edition Core Rules. No missing rules or evidence gaps exist concerning the core Advance procedure. Specific abilities permitting charging after advancing or altering Advance roll mechanics depend on individual unit datasheets or detachment rules.

Section: Hints and Tips DICE ROLLING
In a game of Warhammer 40,000 you and your opponent will be rolling, and in some cases re-rolling, lots of dice. It is good practice to always make sure your opponent knows what you are rolling dice for, and what abilities and rules are in effect that enable you to make any re-rolls.

Many gamers roll their dice somewhere on the battlefield, but some roll their dice elsewhere, such as in a dice tray. Wherever you roll your dice, make sure you roll the dice where your opponent can see the results too. If a dice is rolled out of bounds (i.e. it rolls off your battlefield, out of your dice tray or ends up on the floor), it is very common to ignore the result of that dice and roll it again. Rolling an out-of-bounds dice again doesn't count as having re-rolled that dice.

If a dice does not lie flat on your battlefield after it has been thrown, it is called a cocked dice. Some players use a house rule that unless a dice is flat after it has been rolled, or unless you can balance another dice on top of a cocked dice without it sliding off, it must be rolled again. It is more common for players to roll the dice again only if they can't be sure of the result. In any case, rolling a cocked dice again doesn't count as having re-rolled that dice.

Section: AIRCRAFT IN THE MOVEMENT PHASE

Section: AIRCRAFT AND THE MOVEMENT OF OTHER MODELS
When a unit is selected to move in the Movement phase, if the only enemy models that are within Engagement Range of that unit are Aircraft models, then that unit can still make a Normal or Advance move.

Whenever a model makes any kind of move, it can be moved over enemy Aircraft models as if they were not there, and can be moved within Engagement Range of enemy Aircraft models, but it cannot end that move on top of another model or within Engagement Range of any enemy Aircraft models.

Section: EMBARK
If a unit makes a Normal, Advance or Fall Back move, and every model in that unit ends that move within 3" of a friendly Transport model, they can embark within it. A unit cannot embark if it has already disembarked from a Transport model in the same phase. Remove the unit from the battlefield and place it to one side - it is now embarked within that Transport model. [Core Rules p. 13] (page footer p. 13: CORE RULES | MOVEMENT PHASE)
Section: 1. MOVE UNITS
Start your Movement phase by selecting one unit from your army that is on the battlefield to move:

- Unless that unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can make a Normal move, or Advance, or Remain Stationary.
- If that unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can either Remain Stationary or Fall Back.

After you have finished moving that unit, select another unit from your army to move, and so on, until you have done so with all of your units. Once you have moved all of your units, progress to the Reinforcements step of your Movement phase.

Each time you move a unit, you can move any of its models you choose to. The controlling player chooses the order in which to move their models. Whenever you move a model, you can pivot it and/or change its position on the battlefield along any path, but no part of its base can be moved across an enemy model or cross the edge of the battlefield. It can be moved over friendly models as if they were not there if you wish, but it cannot end its move on top of another model. The only exception to this is when moving Monster or Vehicle models; such models cannot be moved over other friendly Monster or Vehicle models and must be moved around them instead. The distance a model moves is measured using the part of its base that moves furthest along its path. If a model does not have a base, measure using whichever part of that model moves the furthest.

Section: TORRENT
Torrent weapons shoot clouds of fire, gas or other lethal substances that few foes can hope to evade.

[Core Rules p. 25] (page footer p. 25: CORE RULES | WEAPON ABILITIES)
Section: IGNORES COVER
Some weapons are designed to root enemy formations out of entrenched positions.

Weapons with [IGNORES COVER] in their profile are known as Ignores Cover weapons. Each time an attack is made with such a weapon, the target cannot have the Benefit of Cover against that attack (pg 44).

[Core Rules p. 28] (page footer p. 28: CORE RULES | WEAPON ABILITIES)
Section: EXTRA ATTACKS
Some warriors ride to battle atop trusty mounts that gore and trample nearby foes. Others wield combat weapons that deliver a frenzy of additional blows.

Weapons with [EXTRA ATTACKS] in their profile are known as Extra Attacks weapons. Each time the bearer of such a weapon fights, it can make attacks with that weapon in addition to the one it chooses to fight with. The number of attacks made with an Extra Attacks weapon cannot be modified by other rules.

- The bearer can attack with this weapon in addition to any other weapons it can make attacks with.

[Core Rules p. 25] (page footer p. 25: CORE RULES | WEAPON ABILITIES)
Section: RAPID FIRE
Rapid fire weapons are capable of long-ranged precision shots or controlled bursts at nearby targets.

Weapons with [RAPID FIRE X] in their profile are known as Rapid Fire weapons. Each time such a weapon targets a unit within half that weapon's range, the Attacks characteristic of that weapon is increased by the amount denoted by 'x'.

Example: A model targets a unit that is within half range of a weapon with an Attacks characteristic of 1 and the [RAPID FIRE 1] ability. That weapon therefore makes two attacks at the target, and you make two Hit rolls.

- [RAPID FIRE X]: Increase the Attacks by 'x' when targeting units within half range.

Section: 4 WEAPONS
Weapons are described with the following characteristics:

Range: How far the weapon can shoot. Weapons with a range of 'Melee' are melee weapons and can only be used in close combat. All other weapons are ranged weapons.

Ballistic Skill (BS): This shows how accurate the bearer is when shooting with the relevant ranged weapon.

Strength (S): How likely the weapon is to wound a foe.

Armour Penetration (AP): This represents the weapon's ability to cut through the target's defences.

Damage (D): The amount of damage inflicted by a successful wound.

[Core Rules p. 41] (page footer p. 41: CORE RULES | STRATAGEMS)
Section: COMMAND RE-ROLL
1CP

CORE - BATTLE TACTIC STRATAGEM

A great commander can bend even the vagaries of fate and fortune to their will, the better to ensure victory.

WHEN: In any phase, just after you have made a Hit roll, a Wound roll, a Damage roll, a saving throw, an Advance roll, a Charge roll, a Desperate Escape test, a Hazardous test, or just after you have rolled the dice to determine the number of attacks made with a weapon, for an attack, model or unit from your army.

EFFECT: You re-roll that roll, test or saving throw.

[Core Rules p. 9] (page footer p. 9: CORE RULES | CORE CONCEPTS)
Section: RE-ROLLS
Some rules allow you to re-roll a dice roll, which means you get to roll some or all of the dice again. If a rule allows you to re-roll a dice roll that was made by adding several dice together (e.g. 2D6, 3D6, etc.) then, unless otherwise stated, you must re-roll all of those dice again.

You can never re-roll a dice more than once, and re-rolls happen before modifiers (if any) are applied. Rules that refer to the value of an 'unmodified' dice roll are referring to the dice result after any re-rolls, but before any modifiers are applied.

- Unmodified Dice: the result after re-rolls, but before any modifiers.
- A dice can never be re-rolled more than once.
- You must re-roll all dice if several need adding together (e.g. 2D6).
- Re-rolls are applied before any modifiers.

[Core Rules p. 14] (page footer p. 14: CORE RULES | MOVEMENT PHASE)
Section: ADVANCE MOVES
When a unit Advances, make an Advance roll for that unit by rolling one D6. Add the result in inches to the Move characteristic of each model in that unit until the end of the phase. Each model in that unit can then make an Advance move by moving a distance in inches less than or equal to this total, but no model can be moved within Engagement Range of enemy models. A unit cannot shoot or declare a charge in the same turn that it Advanced.

- Advance Move: Models move up to M+D6".
- Cannot move within Engagement Range of any enemy models.
- Units that Advance cannot shoot or charge this turn.

[Core Rules p. 9] (page footer p. 9: CORE RULES | CORE CONCEPTS)
Section: Hints and Tips DICE ROLLING
In a game of Warhammer 40,000 you and your opponent will be rolling, and in some cases re-rolling, lots of dice. It is good practice to always make sure your opponent knows what you are rolling dice for, and what abilities and rules are in effect that enable you to make any re-rolls.

Many gamers roll their dice somewhere on the battlefield, but some roll their dice elsewhere, such as in a dice tray. Wherever you roll your dice, make sure you roll the dice where your opponent can see the results too. If a dice is rolled out of bounds (i.e. it rolls off your battlefield, out of your dice tray or ends up on the floor), it is very common to ignore the result of that dice and roll it again. Rolling an out-of-bounds dice again doesn't count as having re-rolled that dice.

If a dice does not lie flat on your battlefield after it has been thrown, it is called a cocked dice. Some players use a house rule that unless a dice is flat after it has been rolled, or unless you can balance another dice on top of a cocked dice without it sliding off, it must be rolled again. It is more common for players to roll the dice again only if they can't be sure of the result. In any case, rolling a cocked dice again doesn't count as having re-rolled that dice.

Figure label: COMMAND PHASE
Section: THE BATTLE ROUND > COMMAND PHASE
Both players muster strategic resources, then you test your units' battle readiness.

[Core Rules p. 3]
Figure label: 1 COMMAND PHASE
Section: Introduction
1 COMMAND PHASE

2 MOVEMENT PHASE

3 SHOOTING PHASE

4 CHARGE PHASE

5 FIGHT PHASE

In a game as wide-ranging as Warhammer 40,000, there may be times when you are not sure exactly how to resolve a situation that has come up during play. When this happens, have a quick chat with your opponent and apply the solution that makes the most sense to both of you (or seems the most fun!). If no single solution presents itself, you and your opponent should roll off, and whoever rolls highest gets to choose what happens. Then you can get on with the fighting!

[Core Rules p. 11] (page footer p. 11: CORE RULES | COMMAND PHASE)
Section: 1. COMMAND
At the start of your Command phase, before doing anything else, both players gain 1CP. Command points are a strategic resource that you can spend during the battle to use Stratagems. You can find out more about Stratagems on pages 41-42.

Then, if you have any other rules that need to be resolved in the Command phase, you do so now before progressing to the Battle-shock step.

- Both players gain 1CP.
- Resolve any other rules that occur in the Command phase.

Weapons with [TWIN-LINKED] in their profile are known as Twin-linked weapons. Each time an attack is made with such a weapon, you can re-roll that attack's Wound roll.

Section: COMMAND RE-ROLL
1CP

CORE - BATTLE TACTIC STRATAGEM

A great commander can bend even the vagaries of fate and fortune to their will, the better to ensure victory.

WHEN: In any phase, just after you have made a Hit roll, a Wound roll, a Damage roll, a saving throw, an Advance roll, a Charge roll, a Desperate Escape test, a Hazardous test, or just after you have rolled the dice to determine the number of attacks made with a weapon, for an attack, model or unit from your army.

EFFECT: You re-roll that roll, test or saving throw.

Section: RE-ROLLS
Some rules allow you to re-roll a dice roll, which means you get to roll some or all of the dice again. If a rule allows you to re-roll a dice roll that was made by adding several dice together (e.g. 2D6, 3D6, etc.) then, unless otherwise stated, you must re-roll all of those dice again.

You can never re-roll a dice more than once, and re-rolls happen before modifiers (if any) are applied. Rules that refer to the value of an 'unmodified' dice roll are referring to the dice result after any re-rolls, but before any modifiers are applied.

- Unmodified Dice: the result after re-rolls, but before any modifiers.
- A dice can never be re-rolled more than once.
- You must re-roll all dice if several need adding together (e.g. 2D6).
- Re-rolls are applied before any modifiers.

Section: ADVANCE MOVES
When a unit Advances, make an Advance roll for that unit by rolling one D6. Add the result in inches to the Move characteristic of each model in that unit until the end of the phase. Each model in that unit can then make an Advance move by moving a distance in inches less than or equal to this total, but no model can be moved within Engagement Range of enemy models. A unit cannot shoot or declare a charge in the same turn that it Advanced.

- Advance Move: Models move up to M+D6".
- Cannot move within Engagement Range of any enemy models.
- Units that Advance cannot shoot or charge this turn.

Section: Hints and Tips DICE ROLLING
In a game of Warhammer 40,000 you and your opponent will be rolling, and in some cases re-rolling, lots of dice. It is good practice to always make sure your opponent knows what you are rolling dice for, and what abilities and rules are in effect that enable you to make any re-rolls.

Many gamers roll their dice somewhere on the battlefield, but some roll their dice elsewhere, such as in a dice tray. Wherever you roll your dice, make sure you roll the dice where your opponent can see the results too. If a dice is rolled out of bounds (i.e. it rolls off your battlefield, out of your dice tray or ends up on the floor), it is very common to ignore the result of that dice and roll it again. Rolling an out-of-bounds dice again doesn't count as having re-rolled that dice.

If a dice does not lie flat on your battlefield after it has been thrown, it is called a cocked dice. Some players use a house rule that unless a dice is flat after it has been rolled, or unless you can balance another dice on top of a cocked dice without it sliding off, it must be rolled again. It is more common for players to roll the dice again only if they can't be sure of the result. In any case, rolling a cocked dice again doesn't count as having re-rolled that dice.

5 FIGHT PHASE

In a game as wide-ranging as Warhammer 40,000, there may be times when you are not sure exactly how to resolve a situation that has come up during play. When this happens, have a quick chat with your opponent and apply the solution that makes the most sense to both of you (or seems the most fun!). If no single solution presents itself, you and your opponent should roll off, and whoever rolls highest gets to choose what happens. Then you can get on with the fighting!

Section: 1. COMMAND
At the start of your Command phase, before doing anything else, both players gain 1CP. Command points are a strategic resource that you can spend during the battle to use Stratagems. You can find out more about Stratagems on pages 41-42.

Then, if you have any other rules that need to be resolved in the Command phase, you do so now before progressing to the Battle-shock step.

- Both players gain 1CP.
- Resolve any other rules that occur in the Command phase.

Section: TWIN-LINKED
Dual weapons are often grafted to the same targeting system for greater lethality.

Weapons with [TWIN-LINKED] in their profile are known as Twin-linked weapons. Each time an attack is made with such a weapon, you can re-roll that attack's Wound roll.

### Source, Version, and Scope
* **Source:** Warhammer 40,000 Core Rules (10th Edition) [Core Rules p. 9, 13, 14, 15, 17, 25, 41, 54] and Core Stratagem records [DB: stratagems].
* **Supplied Facts:** The user requested the full procedure for making an Advance Move, how distance is determined, and all imposed restrictions.
* **Established Facts:** The rules for selecting units to move, making an Advance roll, model movement, and subsequent restrictions/exceptions on shooting, charging, and Engagement Range are established by the Core Rules citations below.

---

### Process and Rules for an Advance Move

#### 1. Eligibility and Timing
* **Phase & Step:** Performed during the **1. Move Units** step of the Movement phase [Core Rules p. 13].
* **Eligibility:**
  * When selecting a unit on the battlefield to move, it can make a Normal move, an Advance, or Remain Stationary **unless** that unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models [Core Rules p. 13].
  * If a unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can only Remain Stationary or Fall Back [Core Rules p. 13].
  * *Aircraft Exception:* If the *only* enemy models within Engagement Range of the unit are Aircraft models, the unit can still make a Normal move or an Advance move [Core Rules p. 54].

#### 2. Determining the Distance
1. **Advance Roll:** Roll one D6 for the advancing unit [Core Rules p. 14].
2. **Calculate Distance:** Add the result of the D6 (in inches) to the Move (M) characteristic of each model in that unit until the end of the phase [Core Rules p. 14].
3. **Re-rolls:** 
   * A player may spend 1 CP to use the core Stratagem **Command Re-roll** immediately after making an Advance roll to re-roll the die [Core Rules p. 41; DB: stratagems].
   * Re-rolls apply before any modifiers, and a die can never be re-rolled more than once [Core Rules p. 9].

#### 3. Moving the Models
* **Distance:** Each model in the unit can move a distance in inches less than or equal to the combined total ($\text{Move characteristic} + \text{Advance roll}$) [Core Rules p. 14].
* **Path & Positioning:**
  * Models can pivot and change position along any path, measured using the part of the base (or model, if it lacks a base) that moves furthest [Core Rules p. 13].
  * Models cannot cross the battlefield edge and cannot move across enemy models [Core Rules p. 13] (unless the moving model has the **Fly** keyword or is moving over enemy Aircraft [Core Rules p. 15, 54]).
  * Models can move over friendly models (other than Monster or Vehicle models moving over friendly Monster or Vehicle models), but cannot end their move on top of another model [Core Rules p. 13].

---

### Restrictions and Exceptions

1. **Engagement Range:**
   * **General Rule:** No model can be moved within Engagement Range of any enemy models at any point during or at the end of an Advance move [Core Rules p. 14].
   * **Fly / Aircraft Exception:** Models with **Fly** or models moving over enemy **Aircraft** can move within Engagement Range of enemy models/Aircraft during the move, but they cannot end their move within Engagement Range of any enemy model [Core Rules p. 15, 54].

2. **Shooting Restrictions:**
   * **General Rule:** A unit cannot shoot in the same turn that it Advanced [Core Rules p. 14].
   * **Assault Weapons Exception:** If an Advanced unit contains any models equipped with **Assault** (`[ASSAULT]`) weapons, the unit is still eligible to shoot in that turn's Shooting phase; however, it can only make attacks using its models' Assault weapons [Core Rules p. 25].

3. **Charging Restrictions:**
   * A unit cannot declare a charge in the same turn that it Advanced [Core Rules p. 14].

4. **Embarking Option:**
   * If every model in the unit ends its Advance move within 3" of a friendly Transport, the unit is permitted to embark inside that Transport (provided it did not already disembark from a Transport in that same phase) [Core Rules p. 17].

---

### Conclusion & Evidence Gap
All conditions, measurement steps, and restrictions governing Advance moves are defined in the 10th Edition Core Rules. No missing rules or evidence gaps exist concerning the core Advance procedure. Specific abilities permitting charging after advancing or altering Advance roll mechanics depend on individual unit datasheets or detachment rules.
